clue.text: Operatic song from Callas perhaps musicologist initially overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so that letter is dropped from the singer's first name

parts.note: Maria Callas, the soprano, is an example of someone called Maria

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word musicologist

explanation.surface: A critic notes that a certain number sung by the great diva was ignored by a music scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: Callas tempts you to look for a famous role; her first name Maria loses the M from 'musicologist initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo vocal piece in an opera is the standard meaning of the Italian term.

clue.text: Dormant snake has shelter inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the shelter word sits within the snake word

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, Cleopatra's choice
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A hibernating serpent has found a cosy refuge inside something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive as if sleeping, a near synonym.

clue.text: Sell up in game

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to flog is informal British for to sell

explanation.surface: Someone sells up and retires to play a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport, an example of a game played with clubs and balls.

clue.text: Caught leaving English county for a mountainous region of Italy

indicators.note: leaving signals that the letter for caught departs from the county name

parts.note: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught swapping one hilly holiday spot in England for another in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: CUMBRIA is the Lake District county of north-west England; drop its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is the landlocked, hilly central Italian region around Perugia.

clue.text: Highly subtle play on words after penalties

indicators.note: after places the wordplay joke following the penalties

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A referee's witticism follows a series of penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Finespun literally means spun very thin, hence delicate or overly refined.

clue.text: Condiment and perfect herb

parts.note: pepper is a common condiment
in mint condition means perfect, as new

explanation.surface: A cook lists seasoning and a flawless herb.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant is a member of the mint family used for flavouring, so it is a herb.

clue.text: Get on well against Antonio at the end? I did

definitions.text: Get on well against Antonio at the end? I did

indicators.note: against here means right up next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: to prosper is to thrive or get on well

indicators.note: at the end picks out the final letter of the name Antonio

explanation.surface: The speaker claims to have triumphed over Antonio in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest, the deposed Duke of Milan finally gets the better of his usurping brother Antonio, so the whole clue is spoken by him.
explanation.definitionFit: The magician-duke of The Tempest regains his dukedom from his brother Antonio at the play's close.

clue.text: Explicit show

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means clearly stated, as in an ... wish
to show or convey a feeling

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an express instruction is explicit, and to express emotion is to show it.

clue.text: The old lady and I study horse that's never won

parts.note: ma is an informal word for one's mother, one's old lady
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Mother and I study form at the racecourse, backing a winless horse.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a maiden is a horse yet to win a race.

clue.text: Chuffed? Not true

definitions.meaning: British slang for delighted or very pleased
invented or fabricated, as a story might be

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuffed' is everyday British slang for pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both very pleased (British informal) and fictitious or invented.

clue.text: In place of strongholds, indefinitely

parts.note: for can mean instead of, as in swapping one thing for another
keeps are the fortified central towers of castles

explanation.surface: Something replaces castle strongholds for all time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means permanently, with no end date.

clue.text: Head after those who have flogged cheeky young lad

indicators.note: after puts the head word following the floggers

parts.note: whippers are people who whip or flog
napper is old British slang for the head

explanation.surface: An impudent boy gets a clout on the head after a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPPER is dated British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a presumptuous, impertinent young person.

clue.text: A king is after this rare frisky butterfly

indicators.note: after puts the letters for a king following the shuffled ones
frisky means playful and lively, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch pursues a scarce and lively butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisky' rearranges THIS RARE into HAIRSTRE; 'is after' puts A and K behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a family of small butterflies with fine streaked markings on the underwing.

clue.text: Tobacco tin not in use

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
out can mean switched off or not in use

explanation.surface: An old tobacco tin lies unused.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOUT is British prison slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison slang in Britain for tobacco or cigarettes.

clue.text: Before end of decider, draw level

indicators.note: before puts the draw word ahead of the final letter

parts.note: a tie is a draw in a contest

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word decider

explanation.surface: Before the deciding game, the match is drawn level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level' looks like part of the sporting picture but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or layer, one level of a structure.

clue.text: Runner going round course's last turn, one at Aintree perhaps

indicators.note: going round means the runner word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a racer is someone or something that runs in races

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word course

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it's your go

explanation.surface: A horse runs round the bend on the final turn of the course at Aintree.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending a race meeting is a spectator such as a visitor to Aintree.

clue.text: Oscar wearing loose garment in boat

indicators.note: wearing means the garment goes around the letter

parts.note: a slop is an old word for a loose outer garment like a smock
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar, in baggy clothes, is aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Unimaginative experts spies upset

parts.note: pros are professionals or experts

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the spy agency letters upside down

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Dull professionals upset some spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prosaic is matter-of-fact and dull, lacking imagination.

clue.text: Arrest some in revolutionary alliance

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the extracted letters are read backwards
some in means only part of the word alliance is taken

explanation.surface: Police arrest some members of a rebel coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is informal for to catch or arrest them.

clue.text: Doubts, however, beginning in third, harboured by those in boxer's corner

indicators.note: harboured by means the other pieces are held inside the seconds

parts.note: seconds are the attendants in a boxer's corner
though can mean however, as in he did, though

indicators.note: beginning in points to the first letter of the word third

explanation.surface: A boxer's cornermen have doubts about him once the third round starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconsiderations, the misgivings that make you rethink a decision, are doubts.

clue.text: Being kind

definitions.meaning: essential character or existence, as in one's innermost being
sort or type, as in things of that kind

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both essential character and a type or sort.

clue.text: Hotel within reach in poor area

indicators.note: within puts the letter inside the reach phrase

parts.note: to get to a place is to reach it
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: There is a hotel within reach in a poor district.
explanation.definitionFit: A deprived, overcrowded urban district, often of a minority group.

clue.text: Spook just seen in bog

indicators.note: seen in places the fair word inside the marsh

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, a bog
right can mean just or fair

explanation.surface: A ghost has just been spotted on the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spook' looks like a noun (ghost) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spook someone is to scare them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Message American actor Nick left out

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for left is removed

parts.note: Nick Nolte is a US film actor

explanation.surface: A message says the American actor Nick was omitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a short written message.

clue.text: Relaxed American guy

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: An American man is calm and easygoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a noun for a man but is the verb meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortable and free of tension is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Garment seen in Amritsar, India

indicators.note: seen in shows the letters lie within the words Amritsar and India

explanation.surface: A traditional garment is spotted in the Indian city of Amritsar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the long draped dress worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Attendant conserving energy for job

indicators.note: conserving means keeping hold of, so the attendant word holds the letter

parts.note: a carer attends to someone who needs help
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A care worker saves energy to keep the job going.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's occupation or profession.

clue.text: Not saying much, showing discretion about one vase

indicators.note: about means the discretion word goes around the numeral

parts.note: tact is sensitivity or discretion in dealing with others
I is the Roman numeral for one
an urn is a vase-like container

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person is discreet about a single vase.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and uncommunicative.
